correction.text: Wanqiu, 'in present-day Huaiyang County in the plains of eastern Henan province'; 'At its peak, Chen encompassed fourteen cities in modern-day Henan and Anhui'

keyframe_review.note: 5,047 km2 at 113.9-115.44 E, 34.37-34.85 N: the shape lies around Kaifeng, 80 km north of Huaiyang (Zhoukou, 33.63 N in the gazetteer), inside the country of Zheng and Song; Cliopatria's oversized Chu shape (to 34.7 N) covers Huaiyang itself, which is why Chen was drawn displaced (see the Chu dossier). Annexed by Chu 534-529 (ledger). Size right, place wrong.

Valid for 480-479 only, at Huaiyang. region.text: Wanqiu, 'in present-day Huaiyang County in the plains of eastern Henan province'

ledger.note: 1046/45: King Wu enfeoffs Gui Man at Chen. 'After the conquest of the Shang dynasty in 1046/45 BC, King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed his son-in-law Gui Man' as Duke Hu of Chen; infobox 'Established: c. 1045 BC'; 'Its capital was Wanqiu, in present-day Huaiyang County'.

region.text: the State of Chen, made 'a prefecture of Chu'

ledger.note: 534: King Ling of Chu makes Chen a prefecture. 'In 534 BC, the State of Chen suffered internal disorder' (Gongzi Liu 'fled'); 'King Ling made Chen a prefecture of Chu, destroyed its ancestral temple and took Wu back to Chu' (the conversion undated on the page; Chuan Fengxu governs 533-529 in the ruler table). The 598 annexation by King Zhuang in the usual accounts is on none of the pages opened.

529: Chen restored. The King Ling page ends with his suicide in 'winter 529 BC'; the Chen ruler table resumes with 'Duke Hui of Chen 529–506 BC, Ruled for 28 years'. The restoration by King Ping of Chu is not dated on the pages opened; confidence 1.

region.text: Chen, 'fourteen cities in modern-day Henan and Anhui' at its peak

ledger.note: 479: Chu annexes Chen. 'It was finally unified with the Chu in 479 BC'; infobox 'Became capital of Chu: 479 BC'; the Chu page: 'Chu annexed Chen in 479 BC'; the ruler table ends Duke Min in 478. Cliopatria keeps Chen to 451. 'After the destruction of the old Chu capital at Ying, Chen became the Chu capital' (278).

wars.name: Battle of Chengpu
wars.outcome: Jin defeated Chu: 'the Chu kingdom lost their first major battle at the Chengpu in 632 BC'. 'Chen later became an ally state of Chu, fighting as an ally of Chu at the Battle of Chengpu' (Chen page). No Chen land changed hands.

certainty.note: A small fief on the plain south of the Yellow River; no page describes its border, so it is a radius around Wanqiu.

notes: Cliopatria rows to correct: both Chen shapes lie 80 km north of Huaiyang (around Kaifeng) because Cliopatria's early Chu shape covers Huaiyang; the row should end 479, not 451. Not on the pages opened: the 598 annexation by King Zhuang of Chu and its restoration, the 529 restoration by King Ping (confidence 1 from the ruler tables), and the Chen clan's flight to Qi (the page mentions the Tian surname only). Gazetteer name needed: Huaiyang (place, Zhoukou, c. 33.73 N 114.88 E); the dossier uses gazetteer place Zhoukou with a 40 km radius. The Chen page's end year is 479 (text, infobox) against 478 (ruler table).
